slides.headline:
In Jeonju, the rice
is cooked in beef broth.
slides.subline: Gogung, Deokjin-gu — a Jeonju bibimbap house open since 1996, with an exhibition room upstairs

slides.label: the year Jeonju joined the UNESCO Creative Cities Network as a City of Gastronomy
slides.note: It was the first Korean city given that designation. UNESCO's own city profile credits rice from the Honam Plain, fish from the Yellow Sea and mountain greens — and names bibimbap specifically. Source: unesco.org/en/creative-cities/jeonju

items.t: The rice is cooked in beef bone broth
items.d: Jeonju city's official tourism page names this as the defining step — the base is seasoned before a single topping lands on it
Arranged for the harmony of five colours, which is as much about the arrangement as the eating
A regional ingredient that rarely turns up in bibimbap outside Jeollabuk-do. Gogung also sells it as a side dish
Grown locally and prized for the snap. The city lists them among the reasons the dish stayed here

slides.title:
The difference
is under the toppings.
slides.body:
Most bibimbap served abroad is a bowl of plain rice with things placed on top. The Jeonju version starts a step earlier: the rice itself is cooked in beef bone broth, so the base carries flavour before anything is added. Everything above it is arrangement.

That is a difficult thing to notice from a photograph, which may be why Gogung put a bibimbap exhibition room on its second floor — the Korea Tourism Organization's listing describes it as a space explaining the dish's origins and varieties to visitors. A restaurant that thinks the dish needs explaining is a slightly unusual one.

Gogung opened in Jeonju in January 1996 and has since grown to roughly 40 branches nationwide. If you want the room the whole thing started in, it is the Jeonju one.
slides._note: the real message of this post

items.d: The Jeonju main branch, marked by a hanok-style gate. It is in Deokjin-gu, not inside the Hanok Village — plan the trip across town
Listings show no regular closing day, with separate notices at Seollal and Chuseok. Confirm before travelling
Stone pot 16,000 · yukhoe (raw beef) 18,000 · set menus 38,000-55,000. You can ask for a brass bowl instead of a stone pot

slides.text:
This is research, not a personal review.
Every fact here comes from published sources, checked in September 2026.
slides.by:
Gogung is a multi-branch operation of around 40 locations, so if you specifically want a single-room family house, this is not that. We have described what it is rather than ranking it.
Prices and hours change without notice. Taste is always personal.

caption:
Bibimbap abroad is rice with toppings. In Jeonju the rice itself is cooked in beef bone broth first.

Gogung has served Jeonju bibimbap in Deokjin-gu since 1996, and runs a small exhibition room on the dish upstairs. Traditional bowl 14,000 won, open daily 11:00-21:00.

Prices and hours change, so confirm before you go.

Sources in the last slide. Save it for your next trip to Jeonju.
